_about: Papers checked in the systematic screening that began on 22 Nov 2026 (method on about.html#selection). Rendered to checked.html by tools/build.py. Outcomes: clean = no error found; nomaterial = no material error found (checked or rerun); reviewed = method reviewed but data not rerun, no material error found; inprint = already corrected or challenged in print by others; withauthors = finding sent to the authors (count only until they reply or three weeks pass; then add the paper by name, outcome 'flagged', with a link to its register entry); inprogress = check not finished. side: mainstream or questioning (papers questioning mainstream climate findings). 'datasets' and 'code' lists work the same way (no side); flagged datasets and code that are public come automatically from the register (register_rows.json areas 'Observing data' and 'Code' with a 'Real…' verdict, plus custom entries).

We tested whether ranking the 2017–2020 events against a 2000–2020 baseline that contains those same drought seasons could create the reported shift toward conducive fire weather; in a no-trend simulation the effect is under one percentage point.

papers.topic: Global prediction of extreme floods in ungauged watersheds (Google flood forecasting vs GloFAS)
papers.note: Already challenged in print: Li, Razavi, Maier, Hrachowitz et al. 2026, Journal of Hydrology X 30, 100215 (doi:10.1016/j.hydroa.2026.100215) — event thresholds taken from modelled rather than observed flows, a ±2-day hit window, no testing beyond 10-year events, high false-alarm and miss rates, and a single global benchmark. We did not repeat that work.

code.note: Agree within their documented methods; pythermalcomfort and thermal_comfort could mention that their Stull formula is for sea level.

code.topic: Atmospheric radiation scheme (ECMWF IFS, ICON NWP physics)
code.note: Reproduces ECMWF's reference output exactly. Tested with gases set to zero, solver consistency, cloud and sun-angle limits, and doubled vertical resolution.

code.topic: Sea-ice column physics (used by CICE, E3SM and UFS)
code.note: Five-year runs with a seasonal cycle and energy and mass checks switched on: both thermodynamics schemes, three melt-pond schemes, heavy snow, rain on ice, very cold air and summers warm enough to melt all the ice. No conservation failures. The older thermodynamics scheme stops in some melt seasons unless its documented shortwave option is turned on; the documentation already says this.

Ran the 17 priority test cases: variances stayed positive, correlations within bounds, no NaNs. Where the model reports its column-water spurious source (5 of the 17 cases) it is at round-off level, and clipping of negative water is negligible in all cases. Results change at long time steps (20 minutes), but that is already documented in print (Wan et al. 2021, GMD; Santos et al. 2021, JAMES), and the climate models run CLUBB in 5-minute substeps.

code.cite: MOM6 equations of state and freezing point (main, 20 Nov 2026)
code.topic: Ocean model (GFDL, NCAR CESM3) seawater density options
code.note: All eight density options compared with TEOS-10 (GSW) or EOS-80 over temperature, salinity and pressure up to 6000 dbar: differences are the published fitting errors of each formula, the TEOS-10 option matches exactly, and the density derivatives agree with finite differences everywhere. Freezing points agree with TEOS-10. The developers' own documented known bugs (old WRIGHT option, a GSW second-derivative issue) were not counted.
